desks.Dividends: Apple goes ex-dividend Thu Nov 12 at $0.27 per quarter, unchanged; Microsoft goes ex-dividend Thu Nov 19 at $0.98, the first payment at the raised rate (+7.7% from $0.91, its 24th consecutive annual increase), payable Dec 10. Nasdaq's header still shows the stale pre-raise yield of 0.68%; the forward yield is about 0.74%. Nvidia has not yet declared its December dividend. SPY and QQQ December distributions fall outside the window. Tesla pays no dividend.
desks.Earnings: Nvidia is the only watchlist name reporting in the window, Tue Nov 17 after close, with consensus EPS of $2.49 (Nasdaq, 13 estimates) and revenue consensus of about $108.98 billion carried from yesterday's package, not re-verified today. The implied earnings-day move is about 11.2% (about 6-7% event-isolated after corrected time-scaling), against a historical average of about 5% over the last 10 reports. Apple reported Mon Nov 2 after close (EPS $2.10 vs $1.99 consensus); Microsoft reported Oct 28 and Tesla reported Oct 21.
desks.Futures: Brent settled Fri at $98.32 and WTI at $90.83, down about 13% on the week on a same-contract basis — the steepest weekly drop since 2022 — as the midterm result and Qatari mediation repriced de-escalation, while Hormuz transit counts are contested and a Nov 7 closure claim is UNVERIFIED. US crude stocks of 409.8 million barrels sit below every comparable week since 2021, so the selloff is sentiment-led, not inventory-led. Catalysts: USDA WASDE and EIA Short-Term Energy Outlook Tue Nov 10; OPEC monthly Wed Nov 11; EIA petroleum Thu Nov 12 (Veterans Day shift); EIA gas storage and IEA monthly Fri Nov 13.
desks.Parity: No published put-call or box parity violation was found for SPY or QQQ this week. Put-call parity on the 18 Nov options stayed in line with VIX futures settlements on three consecutive closes (Nov 2-4). S&P Dow Jones Indices announced Oct 23 a growth/value classification change, effective before open Mon Dec 21: growth drops 12-month price momentum; value adds free-cash-flow-to-price and an intangibles-adjusted book-to-price. It is a style-index reconstitution only — no change to S&P 500 membership, weighting, or SPX option mechanics, so no parity implication. The current live SPX box-spread rate is UNVERIFIED.
desks.Premium: Saturday post-close implied volatility at the Nov 9 expiry (1 DTE today): SPY 18.0%, QQQ 25.3%, Apple 22.8%, Microsoft 27.1%, Nvidia 49.8%, Tesla 49.0%. A live weekend Yahoo pull runs 4-11 points above those prints on every name with crossed and wide quotes — use the file print as the level. All six verdicts are WINDOW-CONTINGENT — a single day drives 46-63% of each 20-day realized-variance window. Nvidia's Nov 20 expiry implied volatility of about 74.5% versus about 61.0% at Nov 9 is the expected earnings hump ahead of Nov 17; premium into this binary event is to be avoided. Implied-volatility rank is UNVERIFIED for all six names.
desks.Quant lab: Three new candidates were added to the ledger (#235, #236, #237), all WATCH, with no TEST or INTEGRATE movement. #237, a post-earnings-drift decomposition over 81 walk-forwards, finds the unhedged +9.6-point annual spread collapses to +0.1 points once market exposure is hedged. #235 reports a 5.7% RMSE gain on implied-volatility-surface forecasting that fails its significance test (Diebold-Mariano p=0.646). #236 augments HAR realized-volatility forecasts with options-derived rough-volatility inputs. The arXiv q-fin window Nov 6-8 is genuinely empty; the newest item is still 2026-11-05.

items.detail: Nvidia is the only watchlist name reporting in the next two weeks, Tue Nov 17 after close, with consensus EPS of $2.49 (Nasdaq, 13 estimates) and revenue of about $108.98 billion carried from yesterday's package, not re-verified today. The Nov 20 at-the-money straddle implies a move of about 11.2% (about 6-7% event-isolated after corrected time-scaling, down from yesterday's 8.9% which subtracted variances without time-scaling), against a historical average earnings-day move of about 5% over the last 10 reports. The Nov 20 expiry implied volatility of about 74.5% versus about 61.0% at Nov 9 prices the event; premium sold into the print is premium into a binary event: avoid.
items.title: Nvidia reports Nov 17, and options price a move roughly double history

items.detail: Brent fell about 13% on the week on a same-contract basis ($113.43 to $98.32 Fri) and WTI settled at $90.83, the steepest weekly drop since 2022, as the market priced de-escalation after the midterms and Qatari mediation. But US crude stocks of 409.8 million barrels are below every comparable week since 2021, and distillates drew 3.6 million barrels to 99.3 million, a 23-year low — the physical market is tighter than the price fall suggests. Hormuz transit counts are contested (about 2 per day by one measure, 31.5 per day of US-facilitated transits by another) and a Nov 7 closure claim is single-source UNVERIFIED. The next physical check is the EIA petroleum report Thu Nov 12.
items.title: Oil's war premium collapsed on sentiment, not inventories — the physical market is still tight

items.detail: The Thu Nov 5 selloff (SPY -4.51%, QQQ -6.71%, Nvidia -9.72%, Tesla -11.40%) drives 46-63% of each 20-day realized-variance window; the Wed Nov 4 rally (Apple +5.17%, Microsoft +6.47%) drives the other two. Excluding the driver day, realized volatility is SPY 13.4%, QQQ 25.0%, Apple 17.2%, Microsoft 26.0%, Nvidia 37.0%, Tesla 42.4% — every headline 20-day realized figure is inflated by that single day. Implied-volatility rank is UNVERIFIED for all six names — no free IV-history source is available. Verdicts become clean only when Nov 4-5 roll out of the window (about Dec 3-4).
items.title: Every IV-versus-realized verdict is window-contingent — no clean premium call on any name

items.detail: Thursday's front-end rally is the week's rates story: the 2-year fell 12 bp to 4.46% and the 10-year fell 6 bp to 4.84%, steepening 2s10s to +38 bp (FRED, as of Thu Nov 5; Friday's prints were not yet published). SOFR 3.92% against effective fed funds of 3.88% is a 4 bp spread — no funding stress. Tuesday Nov 10 is the week's hinge: October CPI at 8:30 ET, the last CPI the FOMC sees before its Dec 8-9 meeting, alongside USDA WASDE at 12:00 ET and the EIA Short-Term Energy Outlook.
items.title: Front-end rates rallied Thursday; Tuesday Nov 10 is the week's hinge — CPI, WASDE, EIA outlook
